Subject: POC capacity planning - ACME AI

Hi Samir / Aisha,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC capacity planning so we can get your trial environment ready: 

- Success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 250ms for 512-token responses, 99% availability during test windows, and throughput to support ~1200 concurrent chat sessions at peak. We should also validate token-cost per 1k responses.
- Evaluation plan: run a 2-week trial with production-like prompts, measure latency/throughput, and run a 4-hour sustained peak test to exercise autoscaling.
- Capacity ask: you mentioned typical steady-state of ~300 concurrent sessions with spikes up to ~1200 for short bursts.
- Proposed capacity: start with 2 reserved GPU nodes and enable autoscale up to 6 nodes for burst windows; engineering will validate warm-up time and prefix cache behavior.

Next steps:
1) Rishi will propose a concrete GPU sizing and autoscale policy (nodes, instance types, warm pools).
2) I will send the pricing/quote and a short POC runbook (attachments).
3) We'll schedule a 30-min sync next week to finalize timelines (I'm proposing Aug 1 start).

Attaching: poc_capacity_plan_acme_ai_2027-07-25.pdf (draft) and ACME_POCPricing_2027-07-25.xlsx

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple clarifying points from our side before Rishi proposes sizing: 

- The 1200 concurrent sessions peak is accurate but typically lasts ~15-30 minutes during our daily batch pushes. Steady-state is closer to 250-350.
- Our typical prompt length averages 300 input tokens and ~200 output tokens. Latency is critical for our user-facing chat (p95 target <= 300ms ideally).
- Can you confirm what "reserved GPU nodes" means in terms of warm cache and KV reuse? We need short warm-up so bursts don't suffer.

Also, security wise we want to confirm data never leaves our VPC during the trial — we discussed Private deployment earlier; for the trial we can use dedicated pools scoped to ACME.

Happy to join the technical sync when you and Rishi are available.

Samir
Head of Platform — ACME AI
samir.patel@acme.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@acme.ai>

Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 15:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC capacity planning - ACME AI

Hi Samir, great questions, quick technical plan below.

Summary recommendation:
- Baseline: 2 reserved GPU nodes (NVIDIA H100-80GB equivalent) to handle steady-state (~300 concurrent).
- Autoscale: scale up to 6 nodes for bursts (~1200 concurrent). Autoscale configured with fast scaling for short bursts: scale delta +1 node per 30s, with a small warm pool of 1 warm node to reduce cold-start latency.
- Warm cache / KV: we will enable prefix/KV caching per-session and pin hot KV entries to the reserved pool. This reduces warm-up for repeated prompts; cold sessions may still incur first-request penalties (~1s).
- Expected latency: with the above config and batching tuned for 512-token windows, we expect p95 latency ~200-300ms under typical load; we'll instrument and iterate during the first 48 hours.
- Cost/efficiency: quantization profile recommended (int8) for this trial to lower token cost while preserving quality; we can test fp16 if you prefer.

Operational notes:
- Autoscale bursts of 15-30 minutes are expected. To avoid overshoot, we'll use a short smoothing window and rely on a burst quota to prevent oscillation.
- Reservation: reserved nodes guarantee capacity and KV pinning; autoscale nodes are ephemeral and do not hold long-term pinned KV.
- Data: for trial we will provision a dedicated virtual cluster within Redwood Dedicated; traffic stays within your VPC peering (we'll provide the setup steps).

Next steps (technical):
1) Samir / Aisha to share representative prompt set and peak schedule so we can build a load script.
2) We'll run a 4-hour sustained peak test during the trial and share dashboards.
3) Agree on success thresholds and sign the trial start date (Marissa will coordinate).

Attaching a capacity quote and a draft autoscale policy (see attachments). Happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
